descriptionChirho: To meet or encounter someone, often by chance or unexpectedly (Qal). Jacob encountered a place at Bethel (Gen 28:11), angels met him at Mahanaim (Gen 32:1), Moses and Aaron met the Israelite officers (Exod 5:20), encountering an enemy's ox (Exod 23:4), the avenger of blood meeting the manslayer (Num 35:19,21), the spies being encountered (Josh 2:16), borders meeting/joining (Josh 17:10), Saul meeting a band of prophets (1 Sam 10:5), Ruth gleaning without being molested (Ruth 2:22), and God meeting those who do righteousness (Isa 64:5). Arabic uses صَادَفَ/لَقِيَ (to encounter/meet), Korean 만나다 (to meet), Spanish encontrar (to encounter), Hindi मिलना (to meet). This is the basic Qal sense of physical meeting or coming upon.

To reach or touch a geographical boundary, used almost exclusively in Joshua's boundary descriptions (Qal). The tribal borders 'touched' or 'reached' various landmarks: Josh 16:7, 19:11 (twice), 19:22, 19:26, 19:27, 19:34 (twice, including Perf 3ms). Arabic uses بَلَغَ/وَصَلَ (to reach/arrive at), Korean 닿았다 (touched/reached), Spanish tocó/llegó (touched/arrived), French toucha (touched), Hindi छूआ/छूई (touched). This specialized geographic-survey sense is semantically distinct from the general 'meet' sense, as the subject is always an abstract boundary line, not a person.

To strike, attack, or fall upon someone violently, often with lethal intent (Qal). Used of God striking Israel (Exod 5:3), Gideon commanded to fall upon the Midianite camp (Judg 8:21), Ehud's attack (Judg 15:12), execution orders from David and Solomon: 'strike him down!' (1 Sam 22:17-18; 1 Kgs 2:25,29,31,32,34,46). Arabic uses ضَرَبَ/وَقَعَ (to strike/fall upon), Korean 치다/쳤다 (to strike/struck), Spanish golpear/atacar (to strike/attack), Hindi मारना (to kill/strike). Distinguished from the 'meet' sense by the hostile, violent intent and uniform military/judicial context across all occurrences.

To intercede, entreat, or make petition on behalf of another, used in both Qal and Hiphil stems. Abraham asked the Hittites to entreat Ephron on his behalf (Gen 23:8), Ruth told not to press Naomi (Ruth 1:16), Jeremiah forbidden to intercede for the people (Jer 7:16, 27:18, 36:25), the Servant of YHWH intercedes for transgressors (Isa 53:12, Hiphil), no intercessor found (Isa 59:16, Hiphil ptc.), and Isa 47:3 'I will spare no one.' Arabic uses تَوَسَّطَ/شَفَعَ (to mediate/intercede), Korean 중보하다/간청하다 (to intercede/plead), Spanish interceder/rogar (to intercede/plead), Hindi बिनती करना/विनती करना (to entreat). This sense is clearly distinct from physical meeting, evidenced by the Hiphil causative forms (הִפְגִּיעַ, יַפְגִּיעַ, מַפְגִּיעַ) and the uniform prayer/mediation context.

labelChirho: lay upon, cause to light upon
descriptionChirho: Hiphil causative: to cause something to fall upon or be laid upon someone, or to strike a target. In Isa 53:6, YHWH 'caused to fall upon him' (הִפְגִּיעַ) the iniquity of all, and in Job 36:32 God covers his hands with lightning and commands it 'to strike the mark' (בְמַפְגִּיעַ). Arabic uses أَلْقَى (to cast/lay upon) for Isa 53:6 and إصَابَة (hitting/striking) for Job 36:32. Korean 담당하게 하셨느니라 (caused to bear) vs. 치는 자 (the one who strikes). Spanish cargó (loaded upon) vs. intercepta (intercepts). This causative sense of directing or laying something upon a target is distinct from the intercessory Hiphil, representing a physical rather than interpersonal causation.
